title: Scaling Rule Studio & Throughput Audit Explorer
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a focused Console surface that lets operators author and preview autoscaling/throughput rules (the 'Scaling Rule Studio') and inspect a correlated throughput audit explorer. The goal is to reduce misconfigurations, speed up on-call remediation, and surface the causal history of capacity changes for dedicated fleets. This ticket scopes the PM work, acceptance criteria, and handoff to design + eng for the initial MVP.
goals: Provide an editor for autoscale policies with live validation and simulated traffic preview
Expose per-fleet throughput SLOs and effective guarantees alongside historical realized throughput
Create an audit explorer that shows timeline of policy changes, operator actions, automated rollbacks, and correlate with latency/cost and failed requests
Allow safe one-click rollback to a prior policy version and show estimated impact before apply
non_goals: Full RBAC role authoring (will rely on existing RBAC APIs)
Comprehensive historical retention beyond 90 days for MVP
acceptance_criteria: Scaling Rule Studio UI available under Console > Fleets > {fleet} > Controls with Create / Edit / Preview flows
Editor validates rule syntax and warns about common hazards (cascading scale-down, conflicting presets)
Preview simulates 1-minute, 10-minute, and 1-hour traffic patterns and displays expected throughput + latency bands
Throughput Audit Explorer displays a time-aligned view of: policy changes, operator comments, autoscale engine decisions, throughput, latency, and token-cost overlays
Operator can select a prior policy version and initiate a rollback; rollback runs a dry-run simulation and flags potential capacity shortfalls before apply
All UI actions produce an entry in the audit trail with actor, timestamp, diff, and link to the applied commit/PR
notes: Prefer staged rollout UX: save -> dry-run -> apply -> monitor
Need a small schema extension for policy versioning in the control-plane DB; ENG owner is Miguel
Discuss whether preview simulation should run against a sampled request stream or deterministic synthetic traffic
Telemetry: we need a new event type 'policy_preview' to capture estimated impact snapshots for auditability
updates: 2026-03-04 - Kickoff: PM + Design + Eng alignment. Decided on three preview time windows and mandatory dry-run for rollouts.
2026-03-06 - Design: first wireframes posted to Drive. Feedback: add explicit conflict detection between manual operator throttles and autoscale presets.
2026-03-09 - Eng: spike completed for versioned policies and a minimal simulation engine (ENG-41207). Results: simulation within 120ms for 1-minute window on sampled dataset.
2026-03-11 - PM: updated acceptance criteria to include cost overlay and rollback dry-run report. Noted need for SLO metadata to be surfaced in Fleet summary.
2026-03-13 - Design review: accessibility pass scheduled. Small change: move 'Preview' into primary flow (not modal) to improve discoverability.
2026-03-14 - Eng: PR #512 opened for backend schema + policy versioning. Console PR draft created for editor shell. Blocker: audit retention TTL config missing in infra (ENG-41821)
Next: coordinate infra change for TTL, finalize simulation assumptions, and complete design high-fidelity mocks for dev handoff.
risks: Simulation may diverge from live autoscaler behavior; mitigation: run parallel canary comparisons and add confidence metrics
Large fleets could produce noisy timelines — need sensible aggregation and zoom levels in the explorer
Operator confusion if cost estimates are presented without clear assumptions; require explicit model annotations
open_questions: Should the Preview simulation use last-N minutes of real telemetry or a deterministic synthetic generator?
What is the exact retention window for the audit explorer in MVP (90 days vs 180 days)?
Do we allow in-UI edits to multiple rules in a batch or only single-rule transactions?
next_steps: Complete design high-fidelity mocks and handoff tickets to Engineering (due 2026-03-17)
Engineering to finish backend schema PR and simulation engine tests (ENG-41207) and remove infra blocker (ENG-41821)
Schedule cross-team demo with SRE and On-call to validate rollback dry-run behavior (target 2026-03-22)
